app.title: Thematic analysis workbench: AI planning-agent pilot (exit interviews)
app.summary: A researcher reviews an agent's coding of interview transcripts. They walk the coded passages one by one, keep, re-kind, recode or drop each one, and select new spans to code with a definition-aware code picker. They prune the codebook through health filters, a side-by-side compare of two codes and a code-by-code overlap matrix. They check a participants-by-codes coverage grid for gaps and ask for re-reads where cells are empty. Then they drag codes into theme columns, write each theme's brief, and choose the verbatim quotes that go in the paper. Every gesture is applied by a script and logged, and the agent's proposals wait in a pending drawer to be accepted or rejected.

task.text: Build and check a codebook and a set of themes from interview transcripts, ending with the verified quotes chosen for each theme in a paper.

data.text: A corpus of speaker-labelled, timestamped interview transcripts. Coded extracts point into them, and there is a two-level codebook with definitions, themes grouping codes, a participant roster, and optionally screen frames from the recordings.
data.item: an extract: a verbatim stretch of one participant's turn in a transcript, with its codes and a kind (said, did, intent)

stage.text: coding interview transcripts and developing themes from them, through to picking quotes for the write-up

mechanism.text: Tabbed views share one inspector and one pending drawer. The transcript, the codebook, the coverage matrix, the theme board and the quote bank all navigate to the same code, extract or theme by deep link, and the selected item opens in the inspector. Each gesture runs straight away as a logged operation through a script, while the agent's proposals are drawn in place as dashed items that can be accepted or rejected.

field.text: reflexive thematic analysis of interview studies in HCI

workflow.name: code passages of text against an evolving codebook, then group codes into themes and pick supporting quotes

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: The Transcript view tints coded spans by code family and shows a chip per extract. j/k walk the extracts, a accepts and moves on, 1/2/3 set the kind to said, did or intent, x drops, and 'n' toggles a new-only filter.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: Selecting words in a participant's turn opens a bar to make a new extract or re-trim the selected one. Codes are added from a picker that searches ids, names and definitions and shows the definition of the focused code.

The Codebook view lists codes as a two-level tree with health filters such as parent-heavy, only-child, thin and duplicate suspicion. A compare pane sets two codes' definitions over three columns of extracts (only A, both, only B), and an overlap tab cross-tabulates codes by codes.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: The Coverage view shows a participants-by-codes matrix with n/N and a breakdown by kind. Clicking a cell lists its extracts, and clicking an empty cell asks for a re-read of that transcript for that code. Header chips count the codebook version, unapplied edits, transcripts coded and stale transcripts.

The Themes view is a board where code cards are dragged between theme columns. Holding ⌥ or dropping on a column's foot places a code in a second theme too. Each theme gets a brief, a story and its tensions in the inspector.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: The Quotes view lists each theme's bank of extracts with codes, word counts, inline-or-block marks and a frame preview. The researcher chooses and orders the quotes going in and watches how they spread across participants, and selecting words trims a quote to transcript text.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: The Pending drawer lists the agent's staged proposals and comment threads with accept, reject and accept-all, and each item opens where it applies. Resolving a thread closes it.

distinctive: Each extract has a kind (said, did, intent), and hovering a timestamp shows the frame from the screen recording at that moment so a claimed action can be checked
The codebook version counts applications to the transcripts, not edits; edits since the last pass show as unapplied, and transcripts coded before a code changed are flagged as stale
Quotes are only ever copied out of the transcript by script and re-verified, and trimming a quote cuts the stored text rather than letting it be edited
Prevalence is reported per participant as n/N, and an empty cell in the coverage matrix stages a targeted re-read
The agent's proposals are drawn where they would land (dashed theme cards, proposed quotes) and need the researcher to accept them, while the researcher's own gestures apply at once and are logged
